summary.headline: Transrail Q2 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR2,056 crore and EBITDA 28% to INR238 crore (11.6% margin), a record quarter.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue and EBITDA for Q2 FY27 despite Middle East/West Asia disruption to supply chains and logistics. PAT grew only 12% YoY to INR104 crore, which management attributed to a one-off tax charge in September and higher depreciation and interest from capex and working capital funding. Order book stood at INR14,218 crore at September 30, with INR1,747 crore declared post-quarter. Management guided to 20% revenue growth for at least 3 years, annual order intake above INR10,000 crore, and a solar IPP entry via a 49% stake in a 990 MWac Maharashtra project.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR29 crore in H1 FY26

segments.name: EPC / T&D (transmission, substation, conductor)
segments.commentary: Core business; management expects 85-90% of revenue to remain T&D. Order book INR14,218 crore at September 30, with INR1,747 crore declared post-quarter. Domestic/international mix currently about 62:38, targeted at 60:40.

segments.name: Products (towers, conductors sold externally)
segments.commentary: About 95% of tower and conductor output is used internally; external product sales are about 2-5% of revenue, with a stated target of 5-7% for standalone products.

segments.name: Solar IPP (proposed)
segments.commentary: Board approved acquiring 49% of a project SPV for ~990 MWac solar in Maharashtra; project cost about INR3,900 crore, largely debt funded, with INR500 crore equity over the next year. About 400 MW targeted by March/April 2027, full commissioning by March 2028.

guidance_outlook: Annual revenue growth guidance of 20-25%, with management expecting about 20% for at least the next 3 years; further guidance to be given around March/April 2027.
EBITDA margin of 11%+ planned for the current year and following years.
Annual order intake of INR10,000-plus crore with healthy book-to-bill.
PAT margin expected to normalise to 5.5-6% after the one-off tax charge; tax rate expected to return to about 25-26%.
Solar IPP revenue to partly flow from FY28; management said it may revise guidance next year once solar contribution is visible.
QIP: content not finalised, at least 6 months away; enabling Board resolution in place.
Shareholding: 2-3% promoter pledge for short-term borrowing expected to be cleared in 6-9 months.
capex_capacity: Tower manufacturing capacity at 1,84,400 MTPA, with expansion to about 2 lakh MT by end of FY27.
Installed conductor capacity raised to 40,800 km per annum after Phase 1 of conductor expansion; target of about 49,500 km by year-end.
Solar IPP: about 400 MW targeted by March/April 2027; full project commissioning by March 2028.
Epsilon (French carbon-core supplier) building a South India manufacturing facility, expected on stream in about 6 months or more.
BESS and data centre: team being built; BESS results hoped for by end of this year or next financial year.
demand_pricing: Management cites a INR9.15 lakh crore opportunity to 2030-32 and aims to address at least 50% in India; Africa cited as a key international growth market.
Bidding pipeline of about INR30,000 crore over the next 5 months; a bid of about INR18,000 crore is already submitted; 10-12% win ratio assumed.
Five HTLS carbon-core conductor reconductoring jobs won in India (Power Grid in West Bengal and Tamil Nadu); management sizes the opportunity at over INR10,000 crore over 12 months.
Domestic contracts are fully hedged for aluminium and commodity exposure for the year; international jobs carry price variation clauses.
Competition rising from big and small players; management emphasises backward integration, tower test stations and funding quality as differentiators.
Data centre opportunity estimated at INR10,000-15,000 crore per annum, mainly private players; BESS under GEC-III estimated at about INR50,000 crore over 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What peak revenue can be achieved once new capacity is live?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an order book of about INR16,000 crore by year-end as the target to plan for, and said INR12,000 crore revenue by FY29 is achievable at 20% growth. Project durations run 24-30 months.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margins go with 20% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 11%-plus EBITDA margin, with similar margins planned for following years, supported by order book quality.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAT growth (12%) well below EBITDA growth (28%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest cost rose marginally with working capital limits but is falling as a share of revenue. The tax charge was a one-off provided in September; tax rate should normalise to about 25-26%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale and funding for the solar IPP?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar IPP is seen as an adjacent, recurring-revenue business with fixed tariffs. Project cost about INR3,900 crore, mostly debt funded (closed with a large FI), with about INR500 crore equity from internal accruals. Margins expected around 70-80%, per management's broad confirmation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the existing capacity suffice for 20% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity is sufficient for the next 3 years at 20-22% growth, with staggered supply of towers and conductors across projects.

qa_highlights.question: Are domestic contracts exposed to raw-material price moves?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic contracts are fully hedged for the year on aluminium and commodities; cost management is built into margins.

qa_highlights.question: Is there stress in receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO acknowledged an increase in receivables over 6 months (roughly INR200-300 crore range per the questioner) and said it will reduce in the coming quarter.

risks_watch: PAT margin of 5.5-6% vs EBITDA margin of 11%+; depreciation and interest costs rising with capex.
Receivables over 6 months increased; collection trend to be checked next quarter.
Middle East/West Asia crisis affecting supply chain and logistics.
Solar IPP and BESS/data centre entry are new businesses outside core T&D; execution and funding risks, with ~INR500 crore equity requirement.
Tax assessment in progress on the filed return; management said the 14.3% figure included no penalty.
Competitive intensity rising; win ratio assumed at 10-12%.
Order intake target of INR10,000 crore-plus depends on converting the INR30,000 crore pipeline.
Share pledge by promoter of 2-3% to be released within 6-9 months.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, order flow and margins, with repeated emphasis on the record quarter and no guidance misses since listing. Cautious or evasive on specifics: declined to give tower/conductor unit economics, per-km HTLS installation cost and BESS/data-centre order intake, and deferred the multi-year EPS and market-cap questions.
key_quotes: So I'm very pleased to share that Transrail has delivered very strong Q2 '27 performance, recording the highest ever revenue and EBITDA.
Since listing, we have not missed any of our revenue or margin guidance, and we continue to be confident to achieve the same trend this year.
So we're looking at a 20% growth for at least next 3 years, and based on the current plans and the order book.
The margin will definitely come back between 5.5% and 6% going forward.

adds.what: Tower manufacturing capacity expansion to about 2 lakh MT/yr (from 1,84,400 MTPA)
Conductor capacity to about 49,500 km/yr (from 40,800 km/yr after Phase 1)
990 MWac solar IPP (49% stake, Maharashtra); ~400 MW by Mar/Apr 2027, full commissioning by Mar 2028

growth.why: Management guides 20-25% revenue growth (about 20% for at least 3 years) backed by order book of INR14,218 crore plus INR1,747 crore post-quarter, tower capacity rising from 1.84 to about 2 lakh MT by end FY27, and conductor capacity rising to about 49,500 km, though capacity timing is partly uncertain.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin held at 11.6% in H1 and guided at 11%+, while PAT margin is set to fall to 5.5-6% from depreciation, interest and tax normalising to 25-26%; domestic aluminium is fully hedged, so no expansion is signalled.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Tower capacity rising from 1,84,400 MTPA to about 2 lakh MT by end FY27 and conductor capacity from 40,800 to about 49,500 km/yr by year-end, both under construction; 400 MW solar targeted by Mar/Apr 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 20% revenue growth for 3 years, backed by INR14,218 crore order book plus INR1,747 crore post-quarter, and tower and conductor capacity expansion, with capacity seen as sufficient for 20-22% growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is already raised and solar IPP (INR3,900 crore project, INR500 crore equity) is approved; a further BESS or data-centre capex is possible but no firm plan was given, so a new announcement is likely rather than certain.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held revenue growth at 20-25% and EBITDA at 11%+ and said it will only revise guidance around March/April 2027 once solar contribution is visible, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivables over 6 months rose (INR200-300 crore per questioner), PAT margin guided down to 5.5-6% vs EBITDA 11%+, and the Middle East disruption and rising competition (10-12% win ratio) are open risks, though management reports no guidance miss since listing.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: BESS results are hoped for by end of this year or next FY, and the BESS/data-centre team is being built, with BESS under GEC-III sized at about INR50,000 crore over 5 years; timing and order intake were not disclosed.

rows.label: Order intake of INR10,000-plus crore a year
rows.why: Management is confident of INR10,000-plus crore annual order intake against a INR30,000 crore pipeline with a INR18,000 crore bid already submitted at a 10-12% win ratio.

rows.label: Solar IPP 400 MW commissioning
rows.why: Board approved 49% of a 990 MWac Maharashtra SPV with about 400 MW targeted by Mar/Apr 2027 and full commissioning by Mar 2028, with partial revenue from FY28.

rows.label: Receivables collection improvement
rows.why: CFO said over-6-month receivables, which rose by about INR200-300 crore per the questioner, will decline in the coming quarter; NWC held at 82 days for H1.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record quarter, 20% growth, order intake and 11%+ EBITDA margin, but cautious and evasive on unit economics, HTLS per-km cost and BESS/data-centre order intake; analysts pressed on the PAT-EBITDA gap and receivables.
